why: Each servo's degrees are the encoder times a constant; on this bench the constant is off by a different amount on every joint, and the largest error is 12 %. The numbers come from an instrument outside the robot, not from the SDK. A joint also has a deadband: below it the servo does not move and says nothing, which is why one of them is recorded here next to the scale.

shoulder_pan.note: 5.9 % fast; useful travel ends at 116 deg, not the +-170 clamp
shoulder_pan.deadband_basis: measured 2026-11-21: two 0.5 deg steps from the same pose moved nothing, 1.0 deg moved 1.231. The threshold is therefore between 0.5 and 1.0; 1.0 is used as the number a command has to reach. Tick resolution is 0.088 deg, so this is a deadband, not quantisation. Evidence: docs/qualification/baseline/2026-11-21-deadband/

shoulder_lift.note: 1 % slow; about 1 deg of backlash on reversal

elbow_flex.note: fit on shoulder+elbow: the instrument on the forearm reads absolute inclination

wrist_flex.note: two mountings agreeing (0.96 hand-held, 0.937 taped) is what makes this a joint number

wrist_roll.note: 12 % short; only valid read along the axis - oblique readings gave 1.09/1.14/1.24

gripper.note: a percentage is not an angle: J(mm) = 1.346*% + 15.1 opening over 0-50 %, 16 mm at 0 %, 4 mm hysteresis at 25 %. Above 50 % the jaw is a rotating finger, not a parallel gripper.
